Functionalization of 8‑Methylquinolines
Shivam Pandey,<sup>+</sup> Rahul K. Shukla,<sup>+</sup> Atul K. Chaturvedi, and Chandra M. R. Volla*
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2025, 27, 10281−10286

ABSTRACT: Allenes have gained prominence in transition metal-catalyzed C−H activation reactions due to their versatile
reactivity. While C(sp<sup>2</sup>)−H functionalization with allenes has been well explored, the functionalization of more challenging C(sp<sup>3</sup>)−
H bonds with allenes remains largely underexplored. Herein, we present a scalable Rh(III)-catalyzed strategy for the site-selective
C(sp<sup>3</sup>)−H dienylation of biologically relevant 8-methylquinolines employing allenyl carbinol acetates for accessing structurally
diverse 1,3-dienes. Leveraging the innate directing group ability of the quinoline nitrogen, our protocol promotes the selective 2,1-
migratory insertion of allenes. The transformation exhibits a broad substrate scope and enables the late-stage construction of densely
functionalized 1,3-diene conjugates with biologically relevant motifs, highlighting the synthetic utility and broad applicability of this
method.

tional approaches for diene synthesis such as Wittig olefination,
enyne metathesis, and transition metal-catalyzed cross-
coupling reactions rely on prefunctionalized substrates such
as carbonyl compounds, halides, or boronic acids, limiting
modularity and substrate diversity.<sup>3,4</sup> Consequently, strategies
enabling modular access to structurally diverse conjugated
dienes from simple substrates are highly desirable. In this
context, catalytic dienylations leveraging reactive π-systems as
dienylating agents have recently been investigated.<sup>5</sup>
On the other hand, allenes have garnered particular
attention due to their unique structure and versatile reactivity.
In particular, allenyl carbinol derivatives bearing a heteroatom
at the α-position are found to be useful substrates in transition
metal catalysis.<sup>7</sup> The heteroatom guides the insertion pathway
by coordinating with the metal catalyst and facilitates the β-
elimination. In parallel, transition metal-catalyzed C−H
functionalization has emerged as a powerful approach in
organic synthesis, allowing the direct transformation of
otherwise inert C−H bonds into valuable functionalities.<sup>8</sup>

It is worth mentioning that allene having an alkynyl
functionality reacted smoothly as a dienylating agent (22,
88%), keeping the alkyne functionality intact showing the
superior reactivity of allene over alkyne.
We then embarked on exploring the scope of 8-
methylquinolines under the optimized conditions employing
allene 6 to synthesize functionalized 8-methylquinolines
featuring the 1,3-diene motif. Quinolines having a methyl
group at various positions yielded the desired dienylation
products 23−25 in good to excellent yields ranging from 82%
to 89%. Both phenyl and naphthyl groups at the C6 position of
8-methylquinoline were found to be compatible to furnish
dienylated products 26 and
respectively, in 84−87% yields.
However, the use of Br- or Cl-substituted 8-methylquinolines
led to a slight decrease in the yield of products 28−32 (64−
78%). A variety of C3- and C6-alkynylated quinoline
derivatives 33−38 having electron-donating or electron-
withdrawing groups on the alkynyl system were synthesized
in 69−76% yields. Unfortunately, substitution at the C2
position (with methyl or chloro) completely suppressed
reactivity, which might be due to impeding Rh coordination
with the quinoline nitrogen. Interestingly, treating 7-chloro-8-
methylquinoline 40 with 6 provided the desired product 41 in
70% yield. With this observation, we envisioned that this
substrate-dependent reactivity could be exploited in a sterically
selective manner and tested bisquinoline substrate 42 having
two diferent potential sites for the reaction. Pleasingly, when
42 was subjected to the optimized reaction conditions,
monodienylated product 43 was obtained selectively in 65%
yield with the 8-methylquinoline scafold having the 2-Cl
substitution unperturbed.
To demonstrate the applicability of our developed protocol,
allenes tethered with biologically relevant and naturally
occurring alcohol derivatives such as citronellal, β-citronellol,
geraniol, menthol, thymol, cholesterol, and tocopherol were
tested. Conjugated dienes 44−50 were obtained in good yields
of up to 79% (Scheme 3). Owing to the appealing biological
properties of phenothiazine and ethisterone, 8-methylquino-
lines tethered with these entities were prepared and subjected
to dienylation with allenyl carbinol acetates to furnish
conjugates 51 and 52 in 67% and 65% yields, respectively.
Application of our Rh(III)-catalyzed dienylation protocol for
the modular synthesis of conjugates was then assessed by
subjecting 8-methylquinoline tethered with ethisterone and
citronellal-derived allenyl carbinol acetate under the optimized
conditions to isolate complex heterocyclic scafold 53 in 60%
yield. Similarly, cholesterol-conjugated 8-methylquinoline was
coupled with geraniol-derived allene to synthesize 54 in 59%
yield.

ylation of 8-methylquinolines employing allenyl carbinol
acetates via challenging C(sp<sup>3</sup>)−H bond activation in the
absence of any exogenous directing group and ligand. The
innovative use of these reactive allenes opened a new avenue
for expanding the scope of more challenging C(sp<sup>3</sup>)−H bond
activation, and a variety of 8-methylquinoline derivatives were

scafolds. Furthermore, the utility of the developed method-

various synthetic transformations of the product.
